newsitem.title: USA: United Dominion acquires Imo, Core for $770 million.
newsitem.headline: United Dominion acquires Imo, Core for $770 million.

text.p: United Dominion Industries Ltd. will acquire two companies that manufacture pumps and other fluid-control devices for a total of about $770 million, the companies said Thursday.

United Dominion, a manufacturer of industrial and commercial products, will pay about $440 million for Imo Industries Inc. of Lawrenceville, N.J., and about $330 million for Core Industries Inc. of Bloomfield Hills, Mich., including the assumption of debt.
After the transactions are completed, United Dominion will have revenues of about $2.4 billion and about 14,100 employees at 92 locations in 18 countries, it said.

The deals complete United Dominion's transformation to a company focused solely on the manufacture of proprietary engineered products for worldwide industrial markets, the Charlotte, N.C.-based company said.

Recently, United Dominion announced the divestiture of business units in its building products segment, including Varco-Pruden, Windsor Door, and its 50 percent interest in Centria. The divestitures accounted for about $455 million of United Dominion's 1996 sales.
The new acquisitions are expected to provide additional annual revenues of about $750 million, it said.

"They add leading industrial products to our business mix, vastly expand our current product offerings and provide us with numerous opportunities for expansion domestically and internationally," said William Holland, chairman of United Dominion.
Imo is a global manufacturer of pumps, power transmission equipment, fluid sensors, motion control products and automotive components for niche industrial markets.
The company, which derives about 45 percent of its revenues from international operations, has 3,700 employees worldwide at 30 locations in the United States, Europe and Asia.
Core, which produces specialised industrial products in fluid test, measurement and control and farm equipment, has 1,800 employees at 18 locations.

Through a newly formed subsidiary, United Dominion will begin a tender offer by July 3 for Imo's 17.4 million common shares at a price of $6 a share. It will simultaneously tender Imo's $155 million of debt.
Another newly formed United Dominion subsidiary will begin a tender offer for Core's 11.1 million common shares at $25 apiece.

"There has been a lot of interest in valve and pump companies," said Alexander Blanton, analyst with Ingalls & Snyder. "The stocks have not performed well, in some cases because earnings growth has not been startling."
United's purchases are the fourth and fifth fluid technology takeovers in two months.
The multi-billion dollar merger trend began April 21 when ITT Industries Inc. announced its acquisition of Goulds Pumps Inc. for $815 million, plus assumption of $119 million in debt.
On May 6, Durco International Inc. and BW/IP Inc. said they would merge in a stock swap to create a company with a market capitalisation of $1.2 billion.
Two weeks later, Tyco International Ltd announced a $1.2 billion stock swap to acquire Keystone International Inc.
United Dominion's stock fell 31 cents to $25.25; Imo rose $2.625 to $5.75; and Core gained $1.44 to $24.69, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
